items.title: Punjab government opposes Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra's elevation as High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Punjab cabinet on Sunday passed a resolution against the Central government decision to notify the appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra as the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended Justice Mishra’s elevation on August 6. The Central government cleared the recommendation on Saturday night and notified Justice Mishra’s appointment as Chief Justice. However, the State government has alleged that the decision was taken without its consent. Justice Mishra is set to be administered the oath of office at Punjab Lok Bhavan in Chandigarh on Monday. Hours before the ceremony, the Punjab cabinet convened an emergency meeting via video conference to protest the Centre’s decision to appoint Justice Mishra as Chief Justice. In a resolution passed following the meeting, the government urged the Governor not to administer the oath to Justice Mishra until the government gives its consent for the same. items.title: The climate blindspot in India’s new labour codes
items.summary: India’s new labour codes, under which the government framed rules for implementation in May this year, do not once mention climate change. This is even as the past 11 years have been the warmest on record , and extreme weather events are becoming more frequent. Experts say this blindspot leads to a lack of protections for workers. While one labour code does include guidelines for workplaces to tackle climate risks, definitions and minimum thresholds mean the majority of Indian workers in small firms and informal work are excluded from protection. Women are particularly vulnerable to climate risks due to a combination of socioeconomic, cultural and occupational factors. In a four-part series, ISignal reviews the impact of heat and the lack of protections on women’s health and livelihoods. items.title: Bengaluru’s parks are under threat
items.summary: What can you do in 20 minutes? If you are in Bengaluru, it could take longer to cover just one kilometre in a car. It could take longer to get a cup of filter coffee. But that’s all the time it took the Karnataka legislature to introduce a law that could dismantle environmental protections for parks. No floor debate. No public conversation. Just a fast-tracked amendment that gives executive committees a permanent key to carve up 5% of any state park. A metro station, a concrete building for the district administration, or a parking lot can be built here. “5%” sounds like a small, harmless number. But let's do the math. Lalbagh spans roughly 240 acres. Five per cent of that is 12 acres. I am not saying this hasn’t been done before. Earlier governments have passed specific, project-by-project exceptions to take park land. But those were individual bypasses, debated on their own merits. This new law creates a blanket, permanent key. For now, after much outrage, CM DK Shivakumar has taken a step back. Promising to ‘reconsider’ the amendment in the upcoming session. items.title: Two bodies including of a child found stuffed in sacks in Attappady river
items.summary: Human remains believed to be those of a woman and a young girl were found packed in three sacks in the Bhavani river at Attappady in Keralam’s Palakkad district on Sunday, September 6. The discovery has prompted the Pudur police to register a murder case and begin an investigation. The sacks were found in the Cheerakkadavu area along the Bhavani river, around 9 km from Agali. Local residents noticed them after the water level in the river receded on Sunday. The river had remained swollen until Saturday, and the sacks are suspected to have become visible only after the water level dropped. Residents who became suspicious of the sacks opened one of them and found what appeared to be two human heads inside. They immediately alerted the police. A police team that reached the spot subsequently examined the other sacks. One contained the headless body of a young girl, believed to be around five years old. The second sack contained the heads of two persons, while another sack, found around a kilometre downstream, contained body parts believed to belong to a woman. items.title: Telangana CM Revanth orders magisterial inquiry into nurse’s rape-murder
items.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the rape and murder of a 21-year-old nurse at a private hospital in Tukkuguda, on the outskirts of Hyderabad. The CM has directed officials to identify any security lapses that may have contributed to the crime. The inquiry will examine the circumstances leading to the incident, security arrangements at the accommodation where the victim was staying, possible negligence by the hospital management, and compliance with prescribed safety norms for women employees, the Chief Minister’s Office said. With the accused already in police custody, CM Revanth directed senior police officials to expedite the collection of forensic and other technical evidence and ensure that a comprehensive chargesheet is filed without delay. He also directed authorities to take steps to have the case tried in a fast-track court to ensure speedy justice for the victim’s family. CM Revanth assured the family of full government support. Ministers Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy and Seethakka had earlier visited the family. The government has also provided financial assistance and sanctioned an Indiramma house to the family. items.title: Delhi PG collapse: Amid recurring accidents, students ask who will fix unsafe buildings
items.summary: “My parents called me worried when this incident happened. I just moved to Delhi for college and this situation has scared me. I hope we are safe,” a first-year student from Shri Venkateshwara College told Newslaundry , requesting anonymity. A resident of Bihar, she lives in one of the many paying guest (PG) accommodations in Satya Niketan, a locality popular with Delhi University students. On the afternoon of Sunday, September 6, a five-storey PG known as Hostel Daze collapsed, trapping several people inside and triggering a frantic rescue operation. Construction or repair work was underway on the ground floor of the building when it collapsed, according to eyewitnesses. Chaos and panic unfolded in the area as students, residents, police, and rescue personnel rushed to the site. Apart from PG residents, construction workers are also feared to be trapped in rubble. At the time of writing this report, 10 had been pulled out, of whom five are dead, according to the police. Those rescued were taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where they were stated to be in critical condition, officials said. The exact number of those still trapped remained unclear. items.summary: Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda is facing strong criticism for his “casteist” remarks towards pourakarmikas (sanitation workers), whom he asked if they deserved to be paid, claiming that there was 30% absenteeism among the workers. On Saturday, September 5, the Minister, who was carrying out an early morning inspection in Horamavu, Ramamurthy Nagar, Agara Lake and other areas to review garbage collection, footpaths, potholes and other issues, interacted with pourakarmikas at Agara Lake. During the meeting, the pourakarmikas demanded job regularisation (permanent jobs), to which Gowda questioned why they should be regularised when there was 30% absenteeism among the workers. “How can we make those who don’t come to work permanent?” he asked. A video of his remarks went viral on social media, prompting criticism from many, while others, such as Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, supported the Minister.
